topic.original: For an established consumer software team shipping an AI-prototyped (non-AI product) MVP within 90 days, under what conditions does moving fast with AI-generated code help versus hurt the company — and through what specific pathways (code comprehensibility decay, hiring signal loss, test-coverage gaps, customer-feedback velocity) does prototype code convert into either validated learning or terminal maintenance burden? Map the explicit tug-of-war between Product (feature velocity), Engineering (code stability), and Finance (growth per dollar) incentives, challenge the assumption that technical debt is always a mistake by specifying measurable thresholds (% LLM-authored code, time-to-rewrite, defect rate) at which messy code flips from survival tool to liability, and propose a falsifiable alignment mechanism that lets the three departments validate the market without building a technical house of cards.
